subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw expose a synchronous, rejectable Plugin SDK config-write hook that is authoritative for all supported configuration writers, and if so what fail-closed, ordering, and timeout contract should govern it?
rationale: This adds a new in-process policy authority over persisted configuration and cannot be safely resolved by a local implementation choice; it affects plugin trust, write availability, recovery, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Sponsor one authoritative hook
options.body: Specify a shared post-validation, pre-persistence hook with typed input, bounded execution, deterministic ordering, and regression coverage for all config writers.

options.title: Keep built-in validation only
options.body: Retain the current schema, preflight, rejected-write, and Doctor safeguards without exposing a plugin veto contract.

options.title: Limit enforcement to agent tools
options.body: Use existing tool interception for agent-originated changes only, accepting that non-tool writers remain outside the policy boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor one authoritative hook
recommendation.body: Specify a shared post-validation, pre-persistence hook with typed input, bounded execution, deterministic ordering, and regression coverage for all config writers.

likelyOwner.reason: The recorded issue discussion already routes the unresolved API direction to the configuration validation/mutation RFC.
